newsitem.title: USA: ITT shares leap on speculation of higher bid.
newsitem.headline: ITT shares leap on speculation of higher bid.

text.p: ITT Corp stock soared above Hilton Hotels Corp's $55 per share bid on speculation that Hilton will raise its offer.
Wall Street also speculated that ITT, a hotel, gaming and entertainent company, will have to devise a clever defense to fend off its rival.
Arbitragers noted a few chinks in ITT's armor, including the lack of a standard defense most companies have in place -- a staggered board of directors.
One arb said Hilton has until February 13 to propose its own slate of ITT directors, but ITT could counter by expanding the board from the current nine members.

"I think the price could go higher. It looks like a typical hostile (offer) and Hilton will be forced to pay more. They will end up bidding against themselves because I can see no white knight out there," an arb said.
A second arb said, "A big issue is who else other than Hilton would buy ITT, and no names come to mind easily."
ITT shares were up 15 at 57-5/8 late Tuesday morning.
ITT may have more leeway to use the courts to block a takeover because it is incorporated in Nevada, a state with tough anti-takeover laws, arbitragers said.

"Nevada law appears to be pretty hostile to hostile acquirers," said an arb. "There are analogies between Nevada law and Pennsylvania law with regard to fiduciary duties and the way they are carried out. Other constituencies in addition to shareholders are considered, like employees and the community, just like Conrail."
He was referring to Conrail Corp's fight against Norfolk Southern Corp, which has made a hostile takeover offer that is higher than CSX Corp's friendly bid for Conrail.
